topic: "Equal consideration" is not the same as a deadline
text:
UCAS does not call 13 January a deadline. It calls it the equal consideration date, and the difference matters in both directions. An application in by then is guaranteed to be looked at. One after it is not rejected automatically — universities may still consider it, against whatever places are left, and many do.

So a student who misses it has not lost the year, and a student who assumes that means it is flexible has misunderstood the competition. Late is worse, and for a popular course it is much worse. Treat it as a real deadline and know that it is not an absolute one.
attribution: UCAS’s own wording on its dates and deadlines page
whatThisIsNot: The 15 October date for Oxford, Cambridge and medicine behaves differently in practice: those courses fill from the applicants who met it, and applying afterwards is close to pointless.
